source.title: On the Necessity of Attention-FFN Split in Vision Transformers
source.authors: Junhyeok Kim; Jinyeong Kim; Jae Wan Park; S. Hwang

record.tranche_reason: Tests how relaxing the Attention–FFN split changes vision-model test accuracy and representation rank across datasets and model scales; these outcomes concern generalization but do not test a listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The study compares ViT, uViT, and xViT on test accuracy and representation rank. It does not test random-label memorization, train–test gaps, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. The cited results of other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures accuracy and representation rank after changing vision-transformer architecture. None of its own results tests V1–V8. Model scaling does not establish widening beyond zero training error; using AdamW, dropout and batch-size scaling does not test their comparative effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that the Attention–FFN separation restricts performance at smaller scales, with the accuracy advantage of uViT shrinking at larger scales. Rigid parameter allocation is their proposed explanation, not a separately established mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a standard ViT with uViT, which replaces alternating Attention and FFN layers with AttenFeed modules, and xViT, which removes the FFN. It uses shared training conditions for architecture comparisons, not a random-label memorization recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Model scale changes the relative test-accuracy outcome; dataset also changes the size of the difference. The iNaturalist Large-scale run used doubled batch size because uViT convergence was unstable.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10/100, uViT exceeds xViT accuracy by 5.47–7.62 percentage points. Normalized ranks are equal or higher, with several ties.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding GELU to an FFN-removed vision transformer improves classification accuracy and can increase representation rank under the tested recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: uViT exceeds ViT accuracy by 5.62–13.99 percentage points at Small scale and 0.68–1.98 points at Base scale. Large-scale differences range from −0.90 to +0.39 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relaxing the Attention–FFN separation improves vision-transformer accuracy at Small scale under the shared recipe; advantages shrink and become mixed at larger scales.

record.problems: The study reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated accuracy or rank comparisons. The experiments are limited to vision tasks; the authors note that uViT may need a specialized training recipe and that its convergence was unstable in the marked iNaturalist run.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4 transfer-learning comparisons and Table 3 attention-map segmentation comparisons are omitted because the task asks for results bearing on the generalization claim and the selected rows capture the study's direct test-accuracy and measured-rank evidence. Additional qualitative attention-map figures do not bear on the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization with the same recipe, and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that change the penalty.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with dataset size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Representation rank is not magnitude-aware sharpness or a train–test gap. The doubled-batch runs report convergence concerns without a batch-size performance ablation. No uncertainty estimates accompany the extracted comparisons. No additional results bearing on V1–V8 appear in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Large-batch generalization gaps and recipe changes.
Removing memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.
